title: backlog.py in the kb's own checkout starts one git process, not several, to find its root
goal: One backlog.py config run in the kb's own checkout (or a worktree of it) starts at most one git process: default_root returns the tool's own checkout without the --show-toplevel and the two --git-common-dir calls when the working directory is under it, or caches its result for the process, so the hooks that start backlog.py on every session pay one git call.

run: import subprocess,sys,os; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import backlog; n=[]; o=subprocess.Popen.__init__; subprocess.Popen.__init__=lambda s,a,*r,**k: (n.append(a) if isinstance(a,(list,tuple)) and a and a[0]=='git' else None, o(s,a,*r,**k))[1]; sys.argv=['backlog.py','config']; sys.stdout=open(os.devnull,'w'); backlog.main(); sys.stdout=sys.__stdout__; assert len(n)<=1, 'git processes: %d' % len(n)

gates.question: How does default_root avoid the git calls in the kb's own checkout?
options: walk up from the working directory to the nearest .git and return the tool root with no git call when it is the tool's own checkout
cache the result for the process
gates.recommendation: walk up from the working directory to the nearest .git and return the tool root with no git call when it is the tool's own checkout
gates.reason: a cache saves nothing since default_root runs once per process
gates.answer: walk up from the working directory to the nearest .git and return the tool root with no git call when it is the tool's own checkout
